title: Software Engineer, CUDA Deep Learning Systems
reason: Stack +60; Title fit +12; Title stack +8; Exp fit +10; US +10
description_preview:
We are looking for an experienced and highly motivated software professional to work on pioneering initiatives and projects at the intersection of CUDA and Deep Learning Systems. As the complexity and scale of artificial intelligence continue to grow, the intersection of advanced deep learning architectures, massive-scale distributed computing, and low-level hardware optimization has never been more critical. Our team is dedicated to exploring and prototyping next-generation ideas that bridge the gap between deep learning algorithms and CUDA, pushing the boundaries of what is possible on modern accelerator architectures. Join our dynamic, research-oriented team to help unlock maximum hardware performance for emerging AI workloads. You will be a crucial member of a highly technical group exploring uncharted territories in model optimization, custom kernel development, and cluster-scale AI systems design. If you are passionate about the fundamentals of deep learning and thrive on squeezing every ounce of performance out of advanced computing systems from a single GPU to supercomputer clusters, we want you on our team!
What You Will Be Doing
Explore, research, and prototype novel systems optimizations for advanced deep learning models at the intersection of high-level DL frameworks and low-level CUDA through modeling, simulation, and silicon prototyping.
Architect and optimize distributed computing systems that scale seamlessly from a single node to massive, cluster-scale supercomputing environments.
Design, implement, and optimize custom high-performance CUDA kernels tailored to emerging neural network architectures and workloads.
Analyze complex hardware-software interactions to identify and resolve performance bottlenecks in both training and inference pipelines.
Collaborate closely with AI researchers, HW and SW architects, kernel and compiler authors and CUDA driver experts to co-design systems and algorithms that improve accelerator compute utilization, memory bandwidth, cross-node network communication efficiency and programmability.
Develop exploratory tools and runtime systems to profile and accelerate new paradigms in deep learning.
Write clean, effective, and maintainable code, ensuring exploratory prototypes can smoothly transition into open-source releases, upstream framework integrations, internal tools, or closed-source commercial products.
What We Need To See
BS, MS, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).
2+ years of relevant industry experience or equivalent academic experience after degree achievement.
Strong proficiency in C++ and Python programming.
Solid background in the fundamentals of Deep Learning with a focus on transformers.
Strong understanding of distributed computing principles, multi-node scaling, and the unique performance challenges of cluster-scale execution.
Proven experience in systems programming, computer architecture, and low-level systems performance optimization.
Familiarity with deep learning accelerator architectures such as the GPU and hands-on experience with CUDA programming, kernel optimization, and workload profiling
Experience profiling and optimizing generative AI models, including but not limited to, pioneering large language models.
Research background in machine learning systems or adjacent fields and experience profiling and optimizing innovative vision models, generative AI architectures, or diffusion models.
A track-record of initiative and willingness to deep-dive on problems across the stack.
Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd
Deep expertise in performance internals and execution graphs of major deep learning training and inference frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX, TensorRT, vLLM, sgLang, Nemo, Megatron).
Hands-on experience with communication libraries (e.g., NCCL, MPI, UCX) and distributed machine learning techniques (e.g., pipeline, tensor, expert parallelism).
Knowledge of numerical methods and low-precision arithmetic (e.g., NVFP4, MXFP4, FP8, INT8) and their impact on deep learning accuracy and performance.
Background in deep learning compilers and ML systems, including graph-level and codegen tools (e.g., Triton, XLA, torch.compile) and highly parallel/RL-style simulation environments.
Experience designing and implementing agentic AI systems applied to complex systems and infrastructure problems.
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 124,000 USD - 195,500 USD.
You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.
Applications for this job will be accepted at least until August 15, 2026.

Develop, maintain, enhance, and support enterprise Java/J2EE web applications using the Spring Framework to ensure reliable business operations.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or related field.

Experience in application deployment, release management, troubleshooting, and production incident resolution.
Strong understanding of Web application architecture, REST API, database integration, and middleware technologies.
Experience with Linux/Unix environments and basic system troubleshooting.
Experience with SQL and relational databases such as Oracle, PostgreSQL, or similar databases.
Experience with software development lifecycle (SDLC) and IT service management processes.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with DevOps practices and tools including CI/CD pipeline, Git, Jenkins, Kubernetes, or cloud-based deployment environments.
Experience supporting cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Samsung Cloud Platform (SCP); Cloud certification desirable but not required.
Experience with application monitoring, logging, and performance troubleshooting.
Python scripting and automation experience is highly desirable, with exposure to Generative AI, LLM applications, or AI Agent technologies considered a plus.

About the role:
Every usage-based business eventually asks the same three questions in real time: what has this customer consumed, what are they entitled to, and what should happen next? This team owns the runtime layer where billing state becomes something customers can act on — alerting, spend controls, entitlement checks, and usage analytics.
This is a foundational role. Enterprise and AI customers increasingly treat entitlements, spend controls, and real-time analytics as a single problem rather than three separate features, which makes this one of the highest-leverage areas of Orb's roadmap. You'll help set the direction, the primitives, and the interfaces other teams build against.
The work sits squarely at the intersection of infrastructure and product. On one side, it's real systems engineering: alerts, balances, and entitlement checks computed against actual tiers, credits, and commits, fast and reliably enough to stand behind latency guarantees. On the other, it's a customer-facing product surface where API design, clarity, and getting the primitives right matter as much as the systems underneath. You'll spend as much time understanding what customers are trying to do as you will building the thing that does it.
You'll build the system customers rely on to know, in real time, what's been consumed, what's allowed, and what should happen next — the reactive side that alerts the moment a limit is crossed, and the proactive side that serves live balance and entitlement state on demand. Because it runs against Orb's real pricing, credits, and commits, customers can put it directly in the critical path of their own spend and access decisions — the layer they reach for as they scale.
In this role you will:
Own a product surface end to end — from customer conversations and product design through API design, implementation, and rollout
Design and ship alerting and analytics that are granular, flexible, and fast enough to carry contractual latency SLAs
Build the entitlement and spend-control primitives (credit balances, allocations, usage-percentage alerts, rate limits) that enforce against Orb's real billing state in real time

We are building for teams whose systems must not fail. Our mission is to make high-assurance engineering practical and scalable: to turn decades of research and experience on nationally critical systems into an everyday engineering capability.
We believe formal methods are among the most powerful ways to make AI-generated systems trustworthy. We are working at the frontier where LLMs, automated reasoning, and real hardware and software meet, and we believe that combination will reshape how engineering is done.

We are expanding HOARDE's software formal-methods capabilities. We are looking for engineers who can move between code, specifications, verification tools, product infrastructure, and engineering evidence to make rigorous assurance part of software development.
You might prove properties of existing C, C++, or Rust code; recover a specification from code and documentation; build a compatible replacement; or construct new software from a machine-checkable model. .

Customer, founder, and industry research.

Future financing and fundraising support.

Nginx, reverse proxies, SSL, and DNS

APIs and third-party integrations
Deployment and rollback processes
Credential and secrets management
Monitoring, backups, security, and incident troubleshooting

Interest in working closely with founders, investors, and technology companies.

Apply Here
America is strongest when ability can rise
The right person can change the trajectory of a team, a company, or an entire field.
But most hiring systems are built to avoid mistakes, not to discover extraordinary upside. They rely on the credentials that are easiest to read: the right degree, the right previous employer, or the right personal network. These filters, while convenient, are often very poor proxies for what someone can actually do.
When exceptional ability is missed, the loss is larger than one denied opportunity. A company loses performance. Coworkers lose a force multiplier. Ideas and businesses that could have existed never get built. A country that mistakes pedigree for ability does not merely distribute opportunity unfairly, it leaves growth on the table.
History suggests that better talent allocation has been a major source of American growth. When capable people reach the work where they can contribute most, workers rise, companies become more productive, and the benefits can spread through new ideas, stronger teams, families, and communities.
MeritFirst is building the infrastructure to make that the
default
. We create objective, efficient ways for people to demonstrate critical thinking, problem-solving, adaptability, and execution - and help companies hire based on demonstrated ability rather than pedigree alone.
For the worker, that means upward mobility. For the company, better performance. At scale, it can mean national growth.
The role
MeritFirst’s product has to do something much harder than move information around: it has to create a signal that deserves to influence consequential decisions about people.
Candidates must trust that they have a fair opportunity to demonstrate what they can do. Employers must trust that the resulting signal predicts performance better than the credentials they already use. Earning that trust requires exceptional product judgment, rigorous measurement, and software that is reliable, explainable, and built with care.
We’re looking for Software Engineers to help build that system from first principles. You will work directly with our founder, product team, candidates, and employers to shape and build the MeritFirst platform - from the candidate experience and assessment engine to employer workflows, evaluation systems, and the infrastructure beneath them.
This is not a role where a roadmap arrives fully specified. You will help determine what should exist, reduce ambiguous problems to their essential parts, ship the first version, observe how it behaves in the real world, and improve it quickly.
One day you may be designing a new assessment experience. The next, you may be debugging an edge case in production, working through an evaluation methodology with an assessment expert, simplifying an employer
workflow
, or deciding which manual process should become software.
AI gives engineers extraordinary new leverage, and we intend to use it. But our standard is not code that looks plausible or was produced quickly. It is a system we understand, can explain, can test, and can trust.
We expect our engineering team to have deep technical foundations while using modern tools to multiply judgment not replace it.
What you’ll build over time
The responsibilities below describe the full mandate of the engineering function over time, not a day-one checklist for one person.
You will begin by taking ownership of the highest-leverage product and technical problems, shipping directly to users, and developing a deep understanding of where software can most improve the candidate-to-hire
loop
. From there, you will help build the systems and engineering team that allow MeritFirst to scale.
Build the core product. Create candidate and employer experiences that make it easy to demonstrate ability, understand the resulting signal, and act on it.
Build a flexible assessment platform. Develop the primitives that allow us to create, deliver, evaluate, and continuously improve rigorous assessments and realistic work challenges across many kinds of roles.
Own problems end to end. Move from understanding the user and shaping the product through system design, implementation, deployment, observation, and iteration. You will own outcomes, not tickets.

Build evaluation systems worthy of trust. Make results consistent, interpretable, auditable, and resistant to gaming. Design appropriate human review, testing, and safeguards into systems that affect real careers.
Close the learning loop. Connect assessment performance, employer decisions, and on-the-job outcomes so the product becomes more useful and predictive over time.
Use AI where it earns its place. Apply models where they materially improve assessment creation, evaluation, or the candidate and employer experience - and build the evaluations and guardrails required to know whether they are actually working.
Make trust a technical requirement. Treat reliability, security, privacy, accessibility, and candidate experience as foundational product properties rather than cleanup work.
Strengthen the technical foundation. Improve architecture, testing, observability, performance, and developer velocity where the business requires it - without prematurely building infrastructure we do not yet need.
Set the engineering standard. Establish the technical judgment, operating habits, and quality bar that future engineers will inherit. Help us identify and recruit the people who should join you.

ABOUT TITAN DYNAMICS
Founded in 2023, we build additively manufactured UAS and software for commercial and defense customers. Our field-tested fixed-wing, multirotor, and VTOL systems deliver combat-proven performance, rapid adaptability, and lower-cost scalability, powered by proprietary technology that can auto-generate UAS designs and enable deployable factories to produce thousands of aircraft wherever they are needed. We design, print, and fly at a pace traditional aerospace can't match.
THE ROLE
Prometheus is the software heart of Titan Dynamics: it takes mission requirements as input and outputs a complete, manufacturable, flight-ready aircraft design, including aerodynamics, structures, avionics placement, documentation and print files. You'll be a core engineer on Prometheus, and you'll contribute across our broader software stack.
At Titan, the design-build-fly loop is measured in hours or days. You'll auto-generate an aircraft, watch it print, see it fly the same day, then feed what you learned back into the next iteration of Prometheus itself.
Outside of Prometheus, Titan maintains several other software suites, such as PPS (Performance Prediction Software) and various Open Source tools. You will have the opportunity to contribute to these codebases and new ones as we expand our solutions.
You'll be one of a small number of engineers with enormous ownership. The software you write will directly generate aircraft that get printed, flown, and fielded.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
• Design and build core Prometheus features: design generation pipelines, performance prediction, geometry handling, and user-facing workflows
• Integrate with technologies that enable Prometheus and our other software to receive an ATO (authority to operate)
• Contribute to our growing open-source software stack such as TitanPlanner, TitanGroundControl and more
• Build internal tooling that accelerates aircraft design, manufacturing, and flight test
• Work directly with aero, electrical, and manufacturing engineers.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
• 5+ years of professional software engineering experience shipping real products (10+ preferred)
• Deep proficiency in Python, with C++ or TypeScript experience welcomed
• Comfort with geometry, math-heavy code, or scientific/engineering computing. You don't need to be an aerodynamicist, but you shouldn't fear a rotation matrix
• Ability to own features end-to-end: scoping, building, testing, shipping, iterating
• Startup mindset: pragmatic, fast, and allergic to unnecessary process

Position Overview
We are seeking an experienced AI Engineer to design, build, and deploy production-grade AI systems that leverage large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and modern vector databases. The ideal candidate will combine strong software engineering discipline with hands-on experience in LLMs, LangChain, Microsoft Agent frameworks, and scalable search and vector storage solutions such as ChromaDB and Pinecone. You will work cross-functionally to turn research and prototypes into reliable, maintainable services that deliver measurable business value.
Key Responsibilities
Design, implement, and maintain end-to-end AI solutions that incorporate LLMs, RAG architectures, and conversational agents.
Develop and extend LangChain-based pipelines and Microsoft Agent integrations to enable multi-turn, context-aware interactions.
Integrate and manage vector databases (ChromaDB, Pinecone) and Azure AI Search to support efficient retrieval and similarity search workflows.
Build robust prompt engineering, context management, and grounding strategies to improve accuracy and reliability of generated outputs.
Implement model evaluation, monitoring, and logging to track performance, latency, hallucination rates, and user feedback in production.
Collaborate with product managers, data scientists, and software engineers to translate business requirements into scalable technical designs.
Write clean, well-tested Python code, APIs, and microservices; participate in code reviews and maintain CI/CD pipelines.
Optimize inference cost and latency through model selection, caching, batching, and infrastructure tuning (including Azure deployments).
Research and prototype new models, tools, and techniques to continuously improve system capabilities and user experience.
Document system design, runbooks, and operation procedures; provide support during incidents and production rollouts.
Qualifications
Bachelors or Masters degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
3+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a minimum of 2 years focused on machine learning or AI systems.
Proven expertise in Python and production software development best practices (testing, CI/CD, version control).
Hands-on experience with LLMs and building applications around them (prompting, fine-tuning, instruction tuning, or adapters).
Practical experience with LangChain and building composable LLM pipelines and agents.
Experience implementing RAG systems and connecting LLMs to external knowledge via retrieval.
Familiarity with Microsoft Agent frameworks and integrating conversational agents into products.
Hands-on experience with vector databases or stores such as ChromaDB and Pinecone.
Experience integrating and tuning Azure AI Search or equivalent cloud search services; comfort working in Azure.
Knowledge of ML/DL frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, and model deployment tools.
Strong understanding of API design, microservices, containerization (Docker), and orchestration (Kubernetes preferred).
Excellent problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to cross-functional teams.
Nice to have: contributions to open-source projects, prior experience in productionizing LLMs at scale, or advanced degree (MS/PhD).
